subject: Migrate billing to yearly prepay — ops checklist & concession ask
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@cerebrolabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Inquiry on switching to annual prepay and concessions

Karthik —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We are evaluating whether to move our usage from monthly invoicing to a yearly prepay to get better unit economics. Two quick asks:

- Can Redwood provide an illustration of term discounts for a 12-month vs 24-month prepay (we're currently ~$55k/mo run-rate)?
- If we commit to a year upfront, how do you typically handle ramp months where we are still testing new features (partial credits / phased usage buckets)?

Procurement will also want an outline of how credits are applied and a sample SOW. Emily is on copy; she handles contracts.

Appreciate a short ops-level checklist we can share internally.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Engineering, Cerebro Labs
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@cerebrolabs.com>
Cc: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@cerebrolabs.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inquiry on switching to annual prepay and concessions

Sanjay / Emily —

Great to hear from you. Short answers up front, then an ops checklist attached: Redwood_PrePay_Term_Summary.xlsx (high-level table).

1) Term discounts: for a customer at your run-rate (~$660k ARR) we typically offer:
   - 12-month prepay: 10% list unit discount + up to $12k onboarding credit for staged ramp
   - 24-month prepay: 17% list unit discount + $25k onboarding credit and fixed discount floors for years 2

2) Ramp months: we do a staged credit approach — 3-month ramp window where we apply a "ramp credit" to invoice accounting so you effectively only pay for baseline usage while testing new features. Credits are burned first against overage.

3) Migration ops: see the checklist in the workbook (billing cutover steps, PO flow, DocuSign SOW link). Typical timeline is 3–6 weeks from signature if you want a soft-start (no infra changes).

If you want, I can propose a tailored concession: 14% on a 12-month prepay with a $15k ramp credit if you can sign within 10 business days. Looping in Marissa for approval on concessions.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik / Marissa —

A few procurement questions from our side before we can move to legal:

- On the ramp credit: is the $15k refundable or applied as a credit against year 1 usage? We prefer credits applied to invoices, not refunds.
- Can you provide an example amortization schedule so our finance team can map the prepay to the P&L?
- We're exploring a phased migration: Q1 limited rollout (10% of traffic), Q2 full rollout. Would Redwood support a staged increase without re-negotiating pricing?

Also attached: an internal template for SOW items we want included (Cerebro_SOW_v2.pdf). Happy to accept a DocuSign SOW + PO approach.

Best —

Head of Procurement, Cerebro Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Migrate billing to yearly prepay — ops checklist & concession ask

Emily —

Answers inline:

- Ramp credit mechanics: credits are applied to invoices during Year 1 (not refundable). We will show the credit as a line item in month-end statements so your finance team can reconcile.

- Amortization: attaching a sample schedule in Redwood_PrePay_Term_Summary.xlsx (tab: amortization_example). We also include a billing stub every month showing recognized vs unrecognized revenue for your accounting + a simple CSV export (license_and_prices.csv) for PO matching.

- Staged migration: supported. Pricing is locked for the committed term; staged ramp won't trigger repricing as long as total committed capacity is not exceeded. We can add a clause for a mutually-agreed increase trigger (e.g., 30% over committed throughput) that requires re-review.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send the DocuSign SOW (standard 12-month prepay with 14% concession + $15k ramp credit applied to Year 1 invoices).
2) You sign SOW + submit PO.
3) Billing team issues credit note schedule and we mark start date for the prepay period.

If you want to accelerate, Ben can approve a slightly larger onboarding credit.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_PrePay_Term_Summary.xlsx (pricing table & amortization example), license_and_prices.csv

- PO submission within 7 business days of sign (we'll aim for 3)

Emily will add a few minor SOW line edits, but we are ready to move forward. Please send the DocuSign link and the final price CSV so procurement can match the PO.

Appreciate the partnership — excited to get this live.
